claim: AIM6 retains the two catalytic His of the PLC-like phosphodiesterase barrel
finding: TM 0.517, 163 CA eq <5 A, RMSD 2.88 A; His120<->GlpQ His36, His156<->GlpQ His78, Glu141<->Glu63, Asp143<->Asp65; 3-point fit RMSD 0.42 A vs 2.66 A for the His118 alternative
context: S. cerevisiae AlphaFold model vs E. coli GlpQ crystal structure
confidence: high for the fold/register; model-based, no experimental AIM6 structure

claim: The catalytic constellation is under purifying selection
finding: His118, His120, Asp122, Tyr123, Glu141, Asp143, His156, Asp210, Lys212 all 117/117 (100%); control Tyr160 5/117 (4.3%); window identity 37.6-99.2%
context: Fungal members of the AIM6 family
confidence: high; pairwise SW alignments, not a curated MSA

citation: This analysis (30 orthologs incl. 10 bacterial genera)
finding: Same 7 positions 30/30 across Streptomyces, Pedobacter, Chryseobacterium, Alistipes and others at 26.8-33.3% identity

citation: This analysis (AF-Q07716 vs 1PTD; GlpQ vs 1PTD control)
claim: AIM6 can be aligned to B. cereus PI-PLC
finding: AIM6 vs 1PTD TM 0.270, no His equivalence <5 A, indistinguishable from the 1TIM control (0.281); GlpQ vs 1PTD itself only reaches 0.322 with the same method
confidence: the PI-PLC limb of the hypothesis is unalignable with this method, not refuted

claim: The two histidines are catalytically essential in the reference enzyme
finding: H32A, H32N, H32Q, H82A, H82N, H82Q, H82D give 10^4-10^5-fold loss of specific activity toward phosphatidylinositol

claim: Only His32 and His82 of six His are required
finding: H32A and H82A inactive; H92A and H61A fully active; pKa 7.6 and 6.9
confidence: high; establishes specificity of the two-His requirement

claim: Catalysis also needs a phosphate-activating Arg
finding: His32 general base, His82 general acid, Arg69 phosphate-activating; AIM6 has Asn121 and no Arg at the equivalent position
confidence: high for PI-PLC; the AIM6 substitution is inference from the model

claim: Loss of either active-site His abolishes function in vivo
finding: Listeria PI-PLC active-site His mutants retain <1% activity and phenocopy the plcA deletion
